senses.sense: A hurtful thing that kills, as the draught given to Paracelsus by his adversaries.

evidence.quote: being Poysoned in his body by his malicious and inhuman adversaries
by an untimely and violent death of a draught of Poyson

senses.sense: The hurtful part set in every thing of the lower world close beside its physick or healing part, to be separated from it; at CH5.37 called a Tartarous Mucilaginous Impurity.

evidence.quote: nothing in this lower world (which is subject to generation and corruption) is so noble but hath Poyson in it selfe and in respect of another very near the Essence or Physick
hath Poyson or a Tartarous Mucilaginous Impurity hard by or close unto the medicine or Physick thereof
Poyson from healing Medicines and Balsoms

senses.sense: The poison God set in the same place as the physick he gave, as a guard over it.

evidence.quote: in the same place or thing where of his MERCY he appoynted plenty of Physick, even there also by the power of his incomprehensible Justice he substituted Poyson to guard it

senses.sense: A venomous power that can overcome another poison: Nature destroys one poison by another, as opium's greater degree of poison overcomes a pestilence's; each poisonous creature holds an antidote to its own poison.

evidence.quote: there is no poysonous Creature but hath in it an Antidote against its own poyson
by the Specifick venemous vertue of the Opium which hath a greater degree of poyson
Thus Nature destroyeth one poyson by another

senses.sense: A name Paracelsus gives, with Tartar, to the excrements of meat and drink that for the most part breed all diseases.

evidence.quote: which Paracelsus comprehendeth under the name of Poyson and Tartar
these Excrements of meat and drink, which for the most part breed all our diseases

senses.sense: A pair God by his Wisdom ordained to be alike good, as a spectacle of Nature to stir men to search out his secrets; the text's example is one man hating another, and the hated covering and curing the defect of the malicious.

readings.reading: Between things in nature: the text calls it a spectacle of Nature and goes on to Nature as the daughter of War.
Between men as the text words it: one man hating another, the hated curing the defect of the malicious.

evidence.quote: God by his Wisdome hath ordained that Sympathy and Antipathy should be alike good, by which spectacle of Nature he would stir up mortall men to contemplate and search out his secrets
that if one man hate another, he that is hated might cover and cure the defect of the malicious
The cause of Simpathy and Antipathy.

senses.sense: The state set against unity, into which man fell at the Fall, departing from unity; in Regeneration it is swallowed up of unity.

evidence.quote: after the transgression and fall from unity to alterity
The Fall of Man and our great evill is to depart from Unity to Alterity.
through Regeneration (alterity being swallowed up of unity)

senses.sense: Of the whole Creature after the Fall: its beauty transplanted, a transplantation which the note says is by the calamity and coming in of sickness upon it.

evidence.quote: the beauty of the whole Creature was transplanted
The transplantation of the Creature is by the calamity and coming in of sicknesse upon it

senses.sense: Of precious stones: metals carried over into stones, which have their colour, form and tincture more or less from metals.

evidence.quote: for they are transplanted Mertalls
precious stones have the Colour, Forme and Tincture more or lesse from Mettalls by formation of the Stars

senses.sense: Of Eve: Adam set over into another.

evidence.quote: Eve is Adam transplanted.

senses.sense: The whole frame of the world, which man is to till and manage by admiration, searching and knowledge of both the visible and invisible Earth.

evidence.quote: we ought to till and manure the EARTH, to wit, the whole frame of the world by admiration, searching into, and knowledge of both the Visible and Invisible (Limus) Earth
that in the fear of God and love of his neighbor he should manage the Earth, recovering what he hath lost

senses.sense: The Earth that is ordered with good husbandry by one who has learned to know God and himself.

evidence.quote: He that hath learned to know God & himselfe hath ordered the Earth with good husbandry

senses.sense: The element earth, from which man's visible body comes; one of the four in the Microcosm.

evidence.quote: The Physicall, Elementary, visible and Tangible body is from the Earth
When the fruits of the Earth, Aire, Water and Fire of the Microcosm are sick

senses.sense: The bodily part of a simple, to be cast away, as against its virtue, which alone is to be taken.

evidence.quote: the body or Earth of Simples is to be cast away
the vertue Heaven or Astrum of it only to be taken

senses.sense: The crystalline Earth in which what is pure of the Elements shall remain, for ever at rest with the saved.

evidence.quote: shall remaine like a pure, cleare, incorruptible and fixed Essence in a serene resplendent Chrystalin Earth, and be for ever at rest with the happy saved Ones

senses.sense: The healing part of a thing, its physick, lying near its poison and got out by separation from husks and impurities.

evidence.quote: nothing in this lower world (which is subject to generation and corruption) is so noble but hath Poyson in it selfe and in respect of another very near the Essence or Physick
that so at least that quickning essence may be got, whose faculty mounts more high and quick being loosed from its chaines

senses.sense: The one Nature that is the essence and matter of all things.

evidence.quote: that one onely Nature the Essence and Matter of all things

senses.sense: The physical essence in physick, which the note says is called Gold.

evidence.quote: This Physicall essence in Phisick is called Gold.

senses.sense: That to which what is pure of the Elements is likened: it shall remain like a pure, clear, incorruptible and fixed essence.

evidence.quote: And all that is of the Virtues and pure Truth and Nature of the Elements, which feare not the Fire of Heaven shall remaine like a pure, cleare, incorruptible and fixed Essence

senses.sense: Said, with a hedge, of the greatest Medicine: it may be the essence of our life.
senses.voice: QUOTED: Phylosophers our predecessors that have been train'd up in Hermes school

evidence.quote: it may be the Essence of our Life

senses.sense: The being of the seed, from which all men after the first proceed.

evidence.quote: the rest proceed from the Being of the seed or Esence

senses.sense: Physick duly prepared, to be preferred before the Hetroclite mixtures of the shops; the text glosses Spagyricall as divinely-distinguishing.

evidence.quote: Reasons why the Spagyrick Physick duely prepared is to be preferd before other Hetroclite mixtures in the shops.
who have not learned so much as their A. B. C. in the Spagyrick Physick
that Spagyricall or Divinely-distinguishing Sanctuary

senses.sense: Metals as fruit of the Elements, created not for man's food but for his physick.

evidence.quote: although they are the fruit of Elements as well as living things and Vegetables, and created, though not for Mans food yet for his Physick

senses.sense: The view, which the author answers, that metals are of no use in physick.
senses.voice: QUOTED: any who out of their simplicity

evidence.quote: that mettalls are of no use in Physick

senses.sense: Perfect metals as the things in which, above all, God has written on Nature with his own finger.

evidence.quote: upon which God hath written with his own sacred finger in sublunary things, but especially in perfect Mettalls

senses.sense: Metals as riches, left to those driven by the desire of being rich.

evidence.quote: leaving the mettalls to those who with an impious hunger, and a thirsty and insatiable desire of being rich

senses.sense: Metals as things changed, their metamorphosis named beside the curing of diseases.
senses.voice: QUOTED: Phylosophers our predecessors that have been train'd up in Hermes school

evidence.quote: in the curing of diseases and the metamorphosis of Mettalls

senses.sense: Metals as the source of the colour and tincture of precious stones, which are metals transplanted.

evidence.quote: precious stones have the Colour, Forme and Tincture more or lesse from Mettalls by formation of the Stars
for they are transplanted Mertalls

senses.sense: The place or subject in which the one seed or the one Nature is, by whose difference it differs and is called animal, vegetable or mineral.

evidence.quote: differ onely in Quality of Place and Receptacle
according to the disposition and variety of the Place and Receptacle
sometimes is called Animall, sometimes Vegetable, sometimes Minerall, according to the diversity of the subject or receptacle

senses.sense: Noun: what the one Nature is to every creature; the narrowest reading is that which gives each creature its own kind.

evidence.quote: which Nature is the Specifick of every Creature

senses.sense: Of a virtue: a thing's own inward power, set against its outward qualities, by which it cures.

evidence.quote: not (as I have said) by their Externall superficiary qualities, but by an Internall, proper, specifick, harmonious, similer virtue
by the Specifick venemous vertue of the Opium which hath a greater degree of poyson
by a specifick and Harmonicall vertue serve to cure and comfort the heart

senses.sense: The spirit that lives in and quickens the whole mass of the world and fills it, called the Power of God; by its working, with the place and receptacle, bodies differ. What is said of it is to be heard without superstition or idolatrous worship, honour going to God alone.

evidence.quote: That universall Spirit which liveth in and quickneth this whole Masse, which worketh all in all, and filleth the whole world
that Power of God, which comprehendeth all the world in it
according to the agitation and operation of the Universall spirit
but this we must hearken to without any superstition or Idolatrous worship, giving honour onely to One God

senses.sense: Agrippa's names for it: the subject of all mirability, the Being not grasped by sense.

evidence.quote: Agrippa calleth it the subject of all mirability, the Ens or Being that cannot be comprehended by sence

senses.sense: Avicen's name for it: the Soul of the world poured into all things.

evidence.quote: it is the Soule of the world powred into all things

senses.sense: The life-spirit in the body: one through the whole body yet varied by its parts, the source of the body's strength, moving the radical humour and nourished by the humours of life.

evidence.quote: Thus also the Spirit of life is united through out the whole body of man, but is various according to parts of the body in which it is.
for the strengthning power of the Human body and of Animalls proceedeth from the spirit of Life
the Native or Radicall Humor which the Spirit of Life moveth or acteth
The Humors of life do nourish the spirit of life.

senses.sense: Said of the Fift Essence: it is truly the spirit of life, piercing all other spirits and one with the spirit of our body.

evidence.quote: it is truly the spirit of Life which pierceth through all other spirits
and is altogether one and the same with the spirit of our body

senses.sense: The spiracle or breathing hole.

evidence.quote: The Spirit of life is the Spiracle or breathing hole.

senses.sense: The medium that joins the lowest things to the highest by harmonious consent, called animal, vegetable or mineral according to the diversity of the subject or receptacle.

evidence.quote: Nature, I say, is that medium which by an Harmonicall consent joyneth the lowest things to the highest
sometimes is called Animall, sometimes Vegetable, sometimes Minerall, according to the diversity of the subject or receptacle

senses.sense: The order and series of God's works, obeying God and borrowing all its virtue from him.

evidence.quote: which is the order and series of Gods works, and obey the power, word and command of God, and borroweth all its vertue and efficacy from him

senses.sense: The one Nature that came forth as the essence and matter of all things and the Specifick of every creature.

evidence.quote: that one onely Nature the Essence and Matter of all things
which Nature is the Specifick of every Creature

senses.sense: The invisible Fire or fiery vigour by which all things are multiplied.

evidence.quote: is the invisible Fire or fiery vigour by which all things are multiplyed

senses.sense: The healing power within the body: the genuine physician of all diseases, the Internall Mummy or inward Balsom, a virtue and not a quality; the physician is her servant and minister.

evidence.quote: Thus Nature is not onely our companion, but our friend and ready helper, it alone being the genuine Physitian of all diseases
Nature her selfe (who is the Internall Mummy or inward Balsom)
because Nature is not a quality but a vertue
by her servant the Physitian
A true Phisitian should be the minister, not a master to Nature

senses.sense: The present order of the world, which gives nothing pure but mixes all things with impurities, to put men in mind to learn chymistry.

evidence.quote: Nature therefore, as it is now, gives us nothing that is pure in the world, but hath mixed all things with many impurities
it might often put us in mind that we should begin to learn the knowledge of Chymistry from our cradles

senses.sense: Nature as a book and a sanctuary whose secrets the true philosophers and physicians read and enter, whose Light teaches like a sound Doctour; Art and Nature consent like mother and daughter, Art imitating her and supplying her defects.

evidence.quote: the Light of Nature, which like a sound Doctour teacheth and instructeth men
the BOOK of NATURE (in which every region is a leaf)
they go into the very inner roomes and Sanctuary of Nature
because Art and Nature, like mother and daughter, consent to each other
Art imitateth Nature and supplyeth its defects

senses.sense: Heraclitus's name for Nature: the daughter of War.

evidence.quote: Heraclitus called Nature the daughter of War

senses.sense: The nature of each thing, which preserves itself and partakes by affinity of the nature of another.

evidence.quote: every Nature is Naturally the best preserver of it selfe
if the nature of one thing did not by affinity partake of the nature of another

senses.sense: The healing part of a thing, which chymistry separates out; at CH3.14 named the Quint-Essence.

evidence.quote: it teacheth to segregate every mystery into into its own reservacle
the Soul the Inhabitant thereof, the Super-elementall mystery the Quint-Essence

senses.sense: The hidden things of God and of Nature, which true philosophers come to understand and imitate and which impostors are unworthy of.

evidence.quote: really to imitate the greatest mysteries and secrets of Nature
his marvellous works, wonders and mysteries which he hath revealed
as ignorant and unworthy of the mysteries of God, and the secrets of Nature
no perfect perception of Mysteries can be attained to
though divine Misteries are far greater than to be set forth by the splendor of mans words

senses.sense: The soul's turning back within itself into the Mind, by which it draws near to God; closed to the academic spirit, open to humility, and not to be spoken of openly in this place.

evidence.quote: If the Soule run back within it selfe and be converted into the Mind it draweth near to God
The Academicall spirit cannot not understand this Mystery
nor may I in this unfit place openly speak more of these Mysteries

senses.sense: The Phylosophers' work, whose matter is had everywhere because it is in every elementated thing.

evidence.quote: the Phylosophers say that the matter of their Mystery may be had every where, because it consisteth in every Elementated thing

senses.sense: First matter, in which all things were created perfect, and last matter, which the Chymist perfects by Fire.

evidence.quote: ALL things in respect of the first matter were created perfect, but the Chymist perfecteth the last matter by Fire

senses.sense: The one Nature as the matter of all things.

evidence.quote: that one onely Nature the Essence and Matter of all things

senses.sense: The gross bodily matter in which a medicine's power lies drowned and hindered, and from which secrets work apart.

evidence.quote: then whilst they are drowned in Matter, which alwayes hindereth and restraineth the power and operation of the Secret
so far as they are yet drowned in a thick grosse matter
Such is the Nature of all Secrets that they worke without the matter and body

senses.sense: The pure matter of a medicine got by separation; and the most simple and incorruptible matter of the Fift Essence or Medicine, generated out of the spirit of this world, that is, the Soul or Spirit of the world.

evidence.quote: that that pure and Christiline matter may be administred to our bodies
it is the most simple Matter which the Best and Greatest Lord generated out of the spirit of this world for the restauration and preservation of Humane Nature
this Medicine is made of the more incorruptible and efficacious Matter that can be under Heaven, that is, the Soule or Spirit of the world

senses.sense: The matter of the Phylosophers' Mystery, to be had everywhere.

evidence.quote: the Phylosophers say that the matter of their Mystery may be had every where, because it consisteth in every Elementated thing

senses.sense: The matter of the Elixer, which Morienes, asked by King Calid, says is of the king himself.

evidence.quote: King Calid who inquired after the matter of the Elixer
It is of thee O King, said he

senses.sense: Lully's matter, got out of a mean and worthless thing.

evidence.quote: he saith that he got his matter out of a mean and worthlesse thing

senses.sense: The matter of the stone, said to be in every thing in respect of the Vegetall Spirit.

evidence.quote: The matter of a stone is said to be in every thing
which is calld the Vegetall Spirit, by whom our matter of a stone goeth beyond the rest

senses.sense: The matter of diseases, which Paracelsus calls Tartar.

evidence.quote: Paracels saith that the Matter, viz. the Tartar of diseases is twofold

senses.sense: The place the matter of the Elixer is found; Morienes says the king is in it, so a man is meant.

evidence.quote: and thou are in its Mine

senses.sense: The mine out of which the Naturall Mercuriality of the four Elements, of little worth, is got by art; the sentence sets that Mercuriality in man.

evidence.quote: Remember that Man is the most noble Creature of all, in whom there is the Naturall Mercuriality of the four Elements
which is of little worth, and may be got out of its Mine by art

senses.sense: The physician and writer whom the author defends against envious physicians; the text uses this name and Paracelsus for the same man. His physick is neither wholly to be rejected nor wholly embraced.

evidence.quote: if Paracelsus speak any thing against those that follow the rule of their Experience
Some of them are so incensed against that Theophrastus
so would he gladly have served Theophraestus for nothing many years
who cast a Serpents eye upon Theophrastus
who have the true medicines prepared according to Theophrastus his minde
neither the Physick of the Ancients, nor that of Theophrastus, is totally to be rejected
Flagae which Theophrastus in his works affirmeth

senses.sense: Would-be philosophers who are impatient of the long work, greedy and boastful like mountebanks, and without the liberal arts; set beside impostors.

evidence.quote: but with much tediousnesse to Phylosophists who are impatient of delay
as those covètous Mountebanks and greedy Phylosophists use to doe
of which those Phylosophists and Imposters are altogether destitute, having not tasted so much as a drop of the Springs of Nature
